key_insight: Algebraic World Model turns interactions with unfamiliar environments into explicit mathematical models that support machine-checked proofs of reachability and impossibility.
engineering_relevance: The framework connects exploratory testing with formal verification, enabling inspectable rules and certified conclusions about modeled system behavior.
method: Explore environments and iteratively test executable Python hypotheses.
Organize hypotheses into typed objects and shared rules, then simplify using category-theory-guided transformations.
Formalize models in Lean 4 to certify winning trajectories and prove goals unreachable.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports kernel-checked impossibility proofs in all six runs across two impossible levels, plus Lean replay of winning trajectories for all 183 levels across 25 public ARC-AGI-3 games.
watch_item: Lean certifies conclusions within the inferred model; their applicability to the environment still depends on the learned rules accurately capturing its mechanics.
paper_title: Algebraic World Model: From Exploration to Proofs
